key_insight: VoxelMap generated accurate 3D respiratory anatomy predictions from 2D C-arm projections in two deformable lung phantoms, with inference times under 15 ms.
clinical_relevance: The approach could augment fluoroscopic guidance during minimally invasive thoracic procedures with continuously updated volumetric information.
method: Trained a deep learning respiratory motion model using 4D cone-beam CT images.
Evaluated withheld respiratory phases in PixelPrint4D and Casper physical phantoms.
Measured image similarity, inference time, and deep-ensemble uncertainty.
evidence_signal: Across withheld phases, SSIM ranged from 0.927–0.943 for PixelPrint4D and 0.969–0.973 for Casper; higher ensemble uncertainty correlated with greater prediction error.
watch_item: These phantom results do not establish patient performance; clinically representative training data and patient studies are still needed.
paper_title: Real-time Volumetric Imaging for Minimally-Invasive Thoracic Interventions: A Deformable Phantom Study
